newsitem.title: DUBAI: Kuwait Mina al-Ahmadi refinery set for maintenance.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait Mina al-Ahmadi refinery set for maintenance.

text.p: Maintenance work will be carried out in November on a crude distillation unit at Kuwait's Mina al-Ahmadi refinery, Gulf oil traders said on Thursday.
The three-week maintenance period at the 420,000 barrels per day (bpd) capacity plant, starting November 3, will shut one of the plant's three crude units, the sources said.
It was not immediately possible to confirm any work programme at the plant from state refiner Kuwait National Petroleum Company (KNPC).
"The Kuwaitis are relaxed about it," a trader said, adding that inventories had been built up at the refinery to meet term and regular spot commitments to the market.
The crude unit affected at Mina al-Ahmadi -- Kuwait's largest refinery -- has a capacity of 170,000 bpd, one trade source said.
Mina al-Ahmadi is a major exporter of middle distillates products such as gas oil (diesel) and kerosene to Asia and the Indian subcontinent.

The work at Mina al-Ahmadi would coincide with maintenance work at the 305,000 bpd Jubail refinery in Saudi Arabia, potentially depressing spot supplies for the rest of the fourth quarter, traders said.
Kuwait's overall refining capacity is 830,000 bpd.
